test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (JSO) 2023 Official Paper-II (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient r_s=1-frac{6Sigmaᵢ₌₁^n d_i²}{n(n²-1)}, the maximum value of Sigmaᵢ₌₁^nd_i² in case of untied ranks is:
solution:
**The correct answer is - __Option 4: 1/3 n(n² - 1)__**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ **

__
 
• **SPEARMAN'S RANK CORRELATION COEFFICIENT__**

 __
 
• The formula for Spearman's rank correlation coefficient is: **r_s = 1 - (6 Σ d²) / (n(n² - 1))__**, where **__d__** is the difference in ranks of each pair of values and **__n__** is the total number of values being compared.
 
• The value of **__r_s__** ranges from -1 to +1, indicating perfect negative and positive correlation respectively.
 
• The maximum value of the sum of squared differences (∑d²) in the formula occurs when the ranks are as different as possible, i.e., in a situation of complete disagreement between the ranks.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__ **

__
 
• **Calculation of Maximum Value of ∑d²__**

 __
 
• The maximum value of **∑d²__** occurs when the ranks are completely reversed, i.e., the largest value is assigned the smallest rank, and the smallest value is assigned the largest rank.
 
• This results in the maximum possible difference between ranks, thereby leading to the maximum value for **__∑d²__** in the numerator.
 
• The correct formula is **__1/3 n(n² - 1)__**, which corresponds to the scenario where the ranks are as far apart as possible.
 
 
 
• **__Rank Correlation Formula Application__**
 
 
• The Spearman's rank correlation coefficient is widely used in cases where the data does not follow a normal distribution and when the relationship between variables is not linear.
 
• The formula applies to both tied and untied ranks, though the maximum value of ∑d² for untied ranks is specific and results in the answer shown in option 4.
